description: Agent Support Operations: submit resolution records with the customer confirmations they answer to: each resolution with its id, the support ticket, the customer, the issue, the moment the ticket was opened, the moment it was marked resolved, the resolution time the record states in hours, the fix the resolution describes and any earlier ticket for the same issue it follows; each confirmation with its id, the support ticket, the moment the customer answered and whether the customer confirmed the resolution or reopened the ticket. The signed report gives the resolutions and the confirmations, each resolved ticket against a reopening by the customer after it, each resolution against the fix it describes, each customer’s resolved tickets for one issue against the earlier ticket each later one names, and each stated resolution time against the ticket timestamps, and counts them, and names divergent resolutions: a ticket marked resolved that the customer reopened, a resolution recorded with no fix described, the same issue resolved again as if new with no earlier ticket named, and a resolution time that does not recompute from the ticket timestamps; then a confirmation naming a ticket the resolution records do not hold and a resolution with no customer confirmation, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No resolutions, no confirmations, or a stated time beside a resolution with no opening or resolution time to the minute leaves those points unverified. Tickets match by letters and digits, customers without case or punctuation and issues by their words with plurals folded, and resolution times count to the tenth of an hour between two moments that carry a time. This reads whether each resolution holds once the customer answers, ticket by ticket. Verdict support_resolution_divergent, support_resolution_partial, support_resolution_unverified or support_resolution_consistent. POST /api/support-resolution-check. Reads the support records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it answers no customer, sends no message and opens, closes or changes no ticket, which stay with the support team, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Support Operations reads support operation records: ticket logs, first response records, resolution records, escalation records, promise records, performance records, backlog records and the support summary, each against the queue record, the stated response commitments, the customer confirmations, the stated escalation triggers, what the records show happened, the stated service commitments, the ticket list or the records beneath it. The family’s ground is support work already done, read across the whole queue: the DiligenceOps support brief reads one support conversation and lists the promises made in it, and the Agent Feedback family reads the loop around feedback on work, while this family checks whether the support operation’s records hold together across tickets. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-support-operations-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-support-operations/.

at.description: When the customer answered, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

outcome.description: The customer confirmed the resolution or reopened the ticket.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

customer.description: The customer name or reference as the record writes it.

issue.description: The issue as the record names it.

opened_at.description: When the ticket was opened, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

prior.description: The earlier ticket for the same issue reference.

resolved_at.description: When it was marked resolved, such as 2026-03-02T09:15:00Z.

stated_hours.description: The resolution time the record states, in hours.
